chunks: Sulaymān ibn ʿAmr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, complained of her eye in the month of Ramaḍān, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her to break her fast and said: “The evening meal of the night is harmful for your eyes.”

key_terms.تُفْطِرَ: to break the fast or not continue fasting
key_terms.رَدِيءٌ: harmful or unsuitable in this context
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, during which fasting is observed
key_terms.عَشَاءُ ٱللَّيْلِ: the evening meal taken at night
key_terms.عَيْنَهَا: her eye; the bodily organ affected by illness
key_terms.ٱشْتَكَتْ: she complained of an ailment or suffering

ai.seo_question: When does illness permit a person to break the fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that illness affecting a person during Ramaḍān may justify breaking the fast. It presents a Prophetic instruction permitting ifṭār when fasting is detrimental to health, here in the case of an eye ailment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1944 - Sulayman ibn Amr narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"Umm Salama (may Allah (swt) be pleased with her) complained of an issue with her eye during the Month of Ramadan. The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) instructed her to break her fast and said: 'The nourishment of the night is restorative for your eyes.'"
